## Module to write
path: ReplicatedStorage/PlotGrowthConfig.luau
purpose: Feature: Visible plot growth: the plot is a big empty floor, and buying upgrades barely changes how it looks. A new server PlotGrowth module listens to purchases and rebirth resets (UpgradeService already calls into Tycoon/CashInService; hook the same purchase point) and builds a themed model on the owner's plot for every owned upgrade, built from parts in the plot's PlotThemes colors and materials (never default grey), each popping in with GameAssets.popIn and a GameAssets.burst: Dropper 2/3/4 become a real dropper machine (a hopper on legs with a glowing nozzle) on the dropper row above the conveyor; Speed 1/2 add chevron arrows that scroll along the conveyor sides; ore tiers add a matching ore pile/crystal cluster beside the collector (silver, gold, diamond); Cash x1.5/x2 add a vault/coin stack with a floating 'x1.5' sign next to the collector; and after the first purchase a low themed wall with corner pillars and lamps rises around the plot edge. On rebirth all growth models are removed with a shrink tween and rebuilt as upgrades are bought again. Bump counter plot_growth_built. -- Pure shared tunables and data for plot growth, with no side effects. It maps each upgrade id in ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades to a growth kind: dropper (slot index 1-3 for Dropper 2/3/4), speed (level 1-2), ore (silver, gold or diamond) or cashmult (label 'x1.5' or 'x2'). The coder derives the ids and kinds by reading Upgrades.luau and must not invent ids. It also holds local offsets relative to the plot anchor for the dropper row slots, the conveyor side chevron lanes, the ore pile spot beside the collector, the vault spot, and the wall ring (half-extents, wall height and thickness, pillar size). Further values are the chevron count and speed, the popIn and shrink durations, and a 'PartsPerModelCap' safety limit. It exposes `kindFor(upgradeId)` returning kind plus params, or nil. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: plot_growth_built.
depends: ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades.luau

### ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades.luau
```luau
-- Upgrades: pure data for the dropper / ore tier / speed / cash multiplier tree.
-- No requires, no side effects. Returns { list = {...}, byId = {...}, ores = {...}, starterCash = n }.
--
-- This table is the SINGLE source of truth for upgrade prices. Shop cards, world pads, the
-- server purchase check, the tutorial text and the HUD "Next:" hint must all read cost from here.
-- Dropper 2 = 10 and Speed 1 (Fast Belt) = 22, matching the design doc and the tutorial text
-- ("the pad costs $10"). The player starts with 0 cash (Config.STARTING_CASH must match), so the
-- first two collected cubes earn the first purchase.
--
-- BUDGET MATH
--   The first cube (Bronze) is worth 5 cash. The player starts with 0 cash, so the first buy
--   (Dropper 2, 10 cash) is earned by the first two cubes (about 4-8 s after claiming a plot),
--   which fills the HUD goal bar before the pad turns green. After that, income is
--   5 cash/s (2 cubes per 2 s cycle x 5 cash), so every following purchase lands 4-24 s apart.
--   Total cost of all 10 upgrades:
--     10 + 22 + 60 + 150 + 300 + 500 + 800 + 1300 + 2200 + 4000 = 9342 cash
--   Income after each milestone (cubes per 2 s cycle x ore value x cash multiplier, per second),
--   and the approximate wait for the NEXT purchase at that income:
--     base                        1 x 5  x 1.0 / 2 =   2.5 /s   (Dropper 2, 10 -> ~4 s)
--     dropper2                    2 x 5  x 1.0 / 2 =   5   /s   (Speed 1, 22  -> ~4 s)
--     speed1                                           5   /s   (Silver, 60   -> ~8 s)
--     tier_silver                 2 x 12 x 1.0 / 2 =  12   /s   (Dropper 3, 150 -> ~12 s)
--     dropper3                    3 x 12 x 1.0 / 2 =  18   /s   (Cash x1.5, 300 -> ~17 s)
--     mult1 (x1.5)                3 x 12 x 1.5 / 2 =  27   /s   (Gold, 500 -> ~18 s)
--     tier_gold                   3 x 30 x 1.5 / 2 =  67.5 /s   (Speed 2, 800 -> ~12 s)
--     speed2                                          67.5 /s   (Dropper 4, 1300 -> ~19 s)
--     dropper4                    4 x 30 x 1.5 / 2 =  90   /s   (Cash x2, 2200 -> ~24 s)
--     mult2 (x2)                  4 x 30 x 2.0 / 2 = 120   /s   (Diamond, 4000 -> ~33 s)
--     tier_diamond                4 x 75 x 2.0 / 2 = 300   /s
--   (speed upgrades only shorten the trip to the collector.)
--
-- Effect shapes:
--   { kind = "dropper",  slots = n }   total active dropper slots after purchase
--   { kind = "tier",     tier = n }    ore tier every dropper spits out (index into ores)
--   { kind = "speed",    mult = x }    conveyor speed multiplier
--   { kind = "cashMult", mult = x }    collector cash multiplier
--
-- Optional presentation fields (read by the client for the purchase celebration):
--   label  = short headline string
--   popup  = RewardPopup text (shown with Win sting, shockwave ring and FOV punch for ore tiers)
--   color  = Color3 for the shockwave ring / popup (ore tiers)
--
-- Every `requires` points at an existing id, so pads reveal progressively.

local list = {
	{ id = "dropper2", name = "Dropper 2", cost = 10, requires = nil, effect = { kind = "dropper", slots = 2 } },
	{ id = "speed1", name = "Speed 1", cost = 22, requires = "dropper2", effect = { kind = "speed", mult = 1.5 } },
	{
		id = "tier_silver",
		name = "Silver Ore",
		cost = 60,
		requires = "dropper2",
		effect = { kind = "tier", tier = 2 },
		label = "Silver Ore",
		popup = "SILVER ORE! $12 per cube",
		color = Color3.fromRGB(205, 210, 220),
	},
	{ id = "dropper3", name = "Dropper 3", cost = 150, requires = "dropper2", effect = { kind = "dropper", slots = 3 } },
	{ id = "mult1", name = "Cash x1.5", cost = 300, requires = "tier_silver", effect = { kind = "cashMult", mult = 1.5 } },
	{
		id = "tier_gold",
		name = "Gold Ore",
		cost = 500,
		requires = "tier_silver",
		effect = { kind = "tier", tier = 3 },
		label = "Gold Ore",
		popup = "GOLD ORE! $30 per cube",
		color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 205, 40),
	},
	{ id = "speed2", name = "Speed 2", cost = 800, requires = "speed1", effect = { kind = "speed", mult = 2 } },
	{ id = "dropper4", name = "Dropper 4", cost = 1300, requires = "dropper3", effect = { kind = "dropper", slots = 4 } },
	{ id = "mult2", name = "Cash x2", cost = 2200, requires = "mult1", effect = { kind = "cashMult", mult = 2 } },
	{
		id = "tier_diamond",
		name = "Diamond Ore",
		cost = 4000,
		requires = "tier_gold",
		effect = { kind = "tier", tier = 4 },
		label = "Diamond Ore",
		popup = "DIAMOND ORE! $75 per cube",
		color = Color3.fromRGB(80, 235, 255),
	},
}

-- Indexed by tier.
local ores = {
	{ name = "Bronze", value = 5, color = Color3.fromRGB(205, 127, 50), material = Enum.Material.Metal, sparkles = false },
	{ name = "Silver", value = 12, color = Color3.fromRGB(205, 210, 220), material = Enum.Material.Metal, sparkles = false },
	{ name = "Gold", value = 30, color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 205, 40), material = Enum.Material.Foil, sparkles = false },
	{ name = "Diamond", value = 75, color = Color3.fromRGB(80, 235, 255), material = Enum.Material.Glass, sparkles = true },
}

local byId = {}
for _, upgrade in ipairs(list) do
	byId[upgrade.id] = upgrade
end

-- Sanity check: every requirement must reference an existing upgrade id.
for _, upgrade in ipairs(list) do
	if upgrade.requires ~= nil and byId[upgrade.requires] == nil then
		warn("[Upgrades] " .. upgrade.id .. " requires unknown id " .. tostring(upgrade.requires))
	end
end

return {
	list = list,
	byId = byId,
	ores = ores,
	-- Starter grant: 0, so the first two collected $5 cubes earn Dropper 2 (10). Keep Config.STARTING_CASH in sync.
	starterCash = 0,
}

```

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull. Keep the second purchase within about 20-30s of idle income, by raising per-item value or lowering the price. Chain the first few upgrades so there is always something affordable to chase in the first minute, with no long dead gaps.
- Starting cash must be strictly below the first upgrade's price, never equal to it. An instant spend gives the player no chase and no sense of what cubes are for. Start slightly below the price so the first few collected cubes earn it, within about 10s. Check starter cash against the first cost in config before finishing.
- The first purchase must actually happen in a short playtest, and its counters (e.g. upgrades_bought) must be above 0. If the report lacks them, the first pad is too hard to find or reach. A highlight or "affordable" counter above 0 with no purchase counter means the pad was reachable in logic but the player never touched it. Put the first pad close to where the player stands after claiming (just off the walking path), and guide the player to it with a beam. Make sure the tutorial step that points to it fires.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Give failure feedback as well as success feedback. A pad, button, shop purchase or rebirth attempted without enough cash, or a shop card whose requirement is not owned, needs a red flash, an audible buzz, a shake and a "Need $N" or requirement toast, debounced to about 1s. Never return silently from a denied Buy handler. A silent denial confuses young players.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally. They must still be easy to find and reach: guide the player to the first pad with a visible beam or arrow.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~6-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback must fire within about 3-5s, never 20s. A spec or acceptance text that says 20s is wrong for playtests, so shorten it and keep the tested window consistent. Claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza. An idle player must still reach the loop quickly.
- Budget the whole first-payout path, not just the claim: claim delay + first spawn + conveyor travel (length / speed) should land the first cash-in within about 3-4s of the claim. Use a short, fast conveyor, spawn the first item immediately on claim, and don't leave this borderline.
- Keep tutorial text consistent with the actual flow (e.g. don't say "walk to a gate" if auto-claim happens within seconds). Tutorial steps must be advanced by events that actually occur, or the player is left without guidance. Add a time-based fallback so a step can't stall. A tutorial_reshown counter above 0 means a step stalled. Give a clear objective from second 0, make the steps lead the player to every key feature (buy pad, shop), and check that the guide beam or arrow actually appears (its census count is above 0). If the census shows beams = 0, the guide is invisible: fix the beam creation (attachments, parenting, target lookup), not just its config.
- Feedback should be audible and visible: use verified sound ids from the shared asset table, not weak built-in rbxasset wavs. Add particles or ambient sparkle, and set the bloom threshold low enough that Neon parts glow.
- Shared effect helpers (burst, shake, sound, FOV punch) only matter if gameplay code calls them. Wire each helper to a real event (collect, buy, rebirth, big upgrade) and check that its counter is above 0 after a playtest. Big moments deserve stronger feedback than routine ones: camera shake, a shockwave ring, or a larger popup. The purchase is the biggest reward moment, so make sure it has a visible and audible effect and a counter. Fire milestone effects only at milestone counts, not on every event. Make the routine collect reward escalate too (bigger burst or louder sound as streaks or tiers grow), so identical feedback for every cube doesn't flatten the loop.
- Keep routine per-event effects cheap and rate-limited. One sound and one burst per cash-in, at most a few per second per player, and reuse a single Sound object where possible. Do not create a new Sound plus several emitters for every cube. Rate limits and cooldowns must apply only to routine effects. Never let them swallow milestone effects, which must fire exactly when the count hits the milestone

```luau
-- PlotGrowthConfig: pure shared tunables and data for visible plot growth. No side effects.
-- Maps each upgrade id from ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades to a growth kind plus params.
-- All offsets are local to the plot anchor (X = along the plot width, Z = depth, Y = up).

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local Upgrades = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Upgrades", 10))

local Config = {}

-- Explicit growth entries keyed by upgrade id (ids come from Upgrades.luau).
local GROWTH = {
	dropper2 = { kind = "dropper", slot = 1 },
	dropper3 = { kind = "dropper", slot = 2 },
	dropper4 = { kind = "dropper", slot = 3 },
	speed1 = { kind = "speed", level = 1 },
	speed2 = { kind = "speed", level = 2 },
	tier_silver = { kind = "ore", ore = "silver" },
	tier_gold = { kind = "ore", ore = "gold" },
	tier_diamond = { kind = "ore", ore = "diamond" },
	mult1 = { kind = "cashmult", label = "x1.5" },
	mult2 = { kind = "cashmult", label = "x2" },
}

-- Drop any entry whose id is not in Upgrades (never invent ids).
if Upgrades and Upgrades.byId then
	for id in pairs(GROWTH) do
		if Upgrades.byId[id] == nil then
			GROWTH[id] = nil
		end
	end
end

-- Dropper row slots (above the conveyor, along the plot).
Config.DropperSlots = {
	Vector3.new(-14, 0, -12),
	Vector3.new(-4, 0, -12),
	Vector3.new(6, 0, -12),
}

-- Conveyor side chevron lanes (local X offsets from conveyor centreline, Z start/end along belt).
Config.ChevronLanes = {
	Vector3.new(0, 0.6, -3.2),
	Vector3.new(0, 0.6, 3.2),
}
Config.ChevronCount = 6
Config.ChevronSpeed = { 6, 10 } -- studs/sec for Speed 1 / Speed 2
Config.ChevronLength = 24 -- length of belt the chevrons scroll over
Config.ChevronSize = Vector3.new(1.6, 0.2, 1.6)

-- Ore pile spot beside the collector.
Config.OreSpot = Vector3.new(16, 0, -6)
-- Vault / coin stack spot next to the collector.
Config.VaultSpot = Vector3.new(16, 0, 6)

-- Wall ring around the plot edge.
Config.Wall = {
	halfX = 28,
	halfZ = 28,
	height = 3,
	thickness = 1.2,
	pillarSize = Vector3.new(3, 6, 3),
	lampSize = 1.4,
}

-- Timing.
Config.PopInTime = 0.45
Config.ShrinkTime = 0.35

-- Safety limit on parts per growth model.
Config.PartsPerModelCap = 40

function Config.kindFor(upgradeId)
	if type(upgradeId) ~= "string" then
		return nil
	end
	local entry = GROWTH[upgradeId]
	if entry == nil then
		return nil
	end
	local params = {}
	for k, v in pairs(entry) do
		params[k] = v
	end
	return entry.kind, params
end

return Config
```
